The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance and energy-effciency of NVMe SSD systems can be improved by considering the runtime behavior of NUMA systems.

the energy efficiency of I/O threads accessing SSDs on NUMAs is a function of the number of threads and their distribution across CPUs, and that a thread scheduler that is aware of this function and the system runtime characteristics can significantly improve the energy-efficiency of such a system.
we should focus on reducing the remote access penalty of I/O threads accessing SSDs rather than reducing the CPU contention penalty when designing energy-efficient thread schedulers for NUMA systems.
